title: Climate Resilience and Environmental Sustainability of Healthcare Facilities in a Rural District of Pakistan: A Mixed‐Methods Assessment Using the WHO Framework
content:
A mixed-methods WHO CRES-HCF assessment of 12 rural healthcare facilities in Matiari, Pakistan, found only medium climate preparedness (33%–67%), with WASH (41%), workforce (37%), and infrastructure (48%) domains weakest, and energy highest (51%). Environmental built-form analysis identified poor ventilation, excessive solar heat exposure, insufficient insulation, and low plinth levels, whereas spatial flood analysis showed 42% of facilities highly flood-exposed and 50% at moderate risk. No facility met full WHO climate-resilience standards, emphasizing the need for context-specific structural upgrades and communication and awareness-raising activities for healthcare workforce.


ABSTRACT

Climate change increasingly threatens healthcare facilities (HCFs), especially in low- and middle-income countries. This study assessed climate vulnerabilities in 12 HCFs (9 primary and 3 secondary) in a rural district Matiari in Sindh, Pakistan, and proposed sustainable interventions. This mixed-methods study (April–July 2025) combined four components, including a quantitative survey with doctors and patients, an HCF assessment using the World Health Organization (WHO) checklists for climate-resilient and environmentally sustainable HCF, environmental simulations of wind and solar exposure, and Quantum Geographic Information System (QGIS)-based spatial flood analysis. All HCFs had a medium level of preparedness (33.4%–66.6% range) with workforce scoring lowest (37%), water, sanitation, and waste management (WASH) (41.3%), infrastructure (48.3%), and energy (51.0%). Doctors reported inadequate climate preparedness training (50%) and poor waste management (80%). Patients’ responses were mixed, with high access to clean water (80%), but frequent power outages (60%). The environmental analysis identified poor ventilation and excessive heat exposure, and spatial flood analysis identified 42% of the HCFs as highly susceptible. No facility met WHO climate-resilience standards, as no specific domain reached a “high” level of preparedness. There is a need for greater attention and investment across all domains to make the HCFs in Pakistan climate resilient.
